Unless I am wrong, and I will stand corrected, I cannot believe that airplanes are going to be transporting this heavy machinery and raw materials. Therefore, I cannot see the relationship between the need for the airport spur and the above discussion.
Similarly, the discussion of the military facilities bears no relation to the need for an airport spur because these facilities are on the far side of the airport with no access to the spur.
All of the above comments are irking, but amusing. It is one of your final statements in the report that maddens me. On page 115 it states, "Since the predicted 1990 noise levels are based on hypothetical assumptions, highway noise abatement measures will not be warranted until the predicted noise levels are actually reached in the future." What kind of irresponsible statement is this? Such a statement puts the department on record as condoning damage to human health. I've lived long enough to realize that it takes a bureaucracy forever and a day to locate a problem and agree that it is a problem. It takes another coon's age before they'll do anything about it. An efficient organization will solve the problem at the beginning, when it's first realized and not wait until later when it will cost more to solve it.
I would like to make one final statement before concluding. I oppose the project. I don't think it is worth the sacrifice to the neighborhood and it's not worth the price. This is the first impact statement that I have studied and I was extremely disappointed in it and in the performance of your division. The continuing thread throughout this impact statement is, we don't have to write this thing, we don't have to comply with these noise standards, your Joe Citizen had better be satisfied with what we do. This is the attitude I would attribute to a spoiled, lazy child. The issue is this: The Division of Highways, the Department of Transportation is charged with the responsibility of protecting the public health and welfare. This has always been the issue and should continue to be so now and forever into the future. The continual reminders on pages 13, 16, 21 and 22 that the Wisconsin Department of Transportation only filed an impact statement on this project because they were afraid of a change in the law, demonstrates to me an attitude incompatible with a spirit of doing what's right for the state's welfare regardless of the difficulties this charge imposes on you. The concluding statement at the end of part five, which I went into great detail about above bears out my worst fears that this is an agency more concerned with expediency than with protecting the public interest.
Very truly yours,
1427 W. Goldcrest
Milwaukee, Wisconsin 53221
